User Guide & Help

What nodrift does

nodrift is a work-hours tracker that runs entirely inside your browser. You press Work when you start, take breaks as you need them, and press End Shift when you are done. nodrift saves the finished day to a permanent Logbook and shows you how the week is adding up.

There is no account, no sign-up and no server. Everything is stored on the device you are using, which also means each device keeps its own separate history.

Your first shift, in three steps

  • 1. Check the Daily Goal. It sits in the top bar and normally fills itself in for you. Change it before you finish the day if it looks wrong.
  • 2. Track the day. Press Work to begin. Press Break when you step away, and Work again when you come back. Only one of the two timers ever runs at a time.
  • 3. End the shift. Press End Shift. A box appears where you can type a short note about what you did — notes are optional — and the day is then written to the Logbook.

The screen on a computer

  • Left side — the tracker. Production Time on top, Break Time underneath, a progress bar between them, and the Work / Break / End Shift buttons.
  • Right side — three tabs. Insights for charts and totals, Logbook for your saved shifts, and Tasks for a separate small stopwatch.
  • Top bar. Your time zone and two live clocks, the Daily Goal, and the theme picker.
  • Bottom toolbar. Backup JSON, Restore JSON, Leaves, Heatmap, this Help guide, Adjust Timer, Settings, and the red Wipe button.

The Copy and CSV buttons are not in the bottom toolbar — they sit in the header of the Logbook and Tasks tabs, so they always export whichever list you are looking at.

The screen on a phone

On a narrow screen nodrift switches to a phone layout that shows one thing at a time, with five buttons along the bottom edge.

  • Timer (the middle button) is the tracker: your two timers, the progress bar and the Work / Break / End Shift buttons.
  • Insights, Logbook and Tasks open the same three views a computer shows on the right-hand side.
  • Settings & Tools (the last button) slides a panel up from the bottom holding the Daily Goal, the time zone, the theme picker and every toolbar button. Close it by tapping the ×, tapping the dimmed area behind it, or dragging the small bar at the top of the panel downwards.

Nothing else changes: it is the same app with the same data, only rearranged to fit. Keyboard shortcuts are the one thing you will not have on a phone.

Where your data is kept

nodrift writes every shift to your browser's own storage, and keeps a second copy alongside it. If a write to the main store is ever lost — a crash, a tab closed mid-save — the spare copy is used to put the missing entries back the next time you open the app.

That safety net protects you from crashes, but not from clearing your browsing data, switching browsers, or moving to a new device. Those erase everything. Download a JSON backup from the toolbar about once a week so you always have a copy you control.

The three buttons

  • Work — starts the shift, or returns to work after a break. Production Time counts up.
  • Break — stops Production Time and starts Break Time. It appears once a shift is running.
  • End Shift — finishes the day and saves it to the Logbook. You are asked for an optional note first. Once saved, the day can still be corrected from the Logbook.

On a computer the space bar does the same job as whichever of these buttons is showing.

The timers and the progress bar

  • Production Time is time spent working. Break Time is time spent away. They never run at the same time.
  • Left of the bar shows how far along you are and how much is left of today's goal.
  • Right of the bar estimates what time you will finish, shown on the fixed BST clock.
  • The bar turns fully green once you reach the goal.

Both timers are worked out from the clock, not by counting ticks. If the browser slows the page down in a background tab, or you lock the screen, the totals are still right when you come back.

Fixing a timer that is wrong

Open Adjust Timer from the toolbar to add or remove time from the current shift — useful if you forgot to press Break, or started late.

  • Pick Work or Break at the top of the popup. Whichever timer is running is chosen for you.
  • Type an amount such as +15m, -5m 30s, 1.5h or 1h 15m 30s. A bare number means minutes.
  • A preview above the popup shows the result before you apply it, and warns you if you type a clock time (like 9:00 AM) instead of an amount.
  • Subtracting more than a timer holds will not produce a negative number. The timer stops at zero and your shift start time moves forward to absorb the rest.
  • After applying, a message with an Undo button appears so you can put the timers straight back.

The Daily Goal

The goal in the top bar is how many hours you are aiming for today. Left alone, it fills itself in to keep you on pace for a 40-hour week.

  • Monday to Friday: the goal is whatever today needs to be for the week to still reach 40 hours. Log 10 hours on Monday and Tuesday asks for 6; log 7 on Monday and Tuesday asks for 9.
  • Saturday and Sunday: the goal is a flat 6 hours.
  • Booked leave earlier in the week takes 8 hours off the weekly total, so the remaining days are not asked to make it up.
  • You can always override it. Click the goal to open the presets, use −15m / +15m, or type a value. Double-click a preset button to save your own amount onto it.

If you would rather set the goal yourself every day, turn Auto-populate daily goal off in Settings. It cannot be switched while a shift is running.

Locked goals and split shifts

When you save the first shift of a day, that day's goal is locked to it. Changing tomorrow's goal will never rewrite yesterday's records.

If you end a shift and start another one on the same day, the goal in the top bar shrinks to show only what is still left of that locked target, so the progress bar stays meaningful for the rest of the day.

To correct a goal you have already locked in, open the Logbook, edit that entry, and change the goal there.

Automatic protections

These run on their own in the background. Idle Lock can be switched off in Settings; the others always run.

  • Idle Lock. If there is no typing, clicking or scrolling for longer than your threshold (1 hour to start with), the timer pauses. When you come back, nodrift shows you exactly how long the gap was and asks whether to Log as Work, Log as Break, or Discard Idle Time.
  • Sleep and suspended tabs. If your computer sleeps or the browser puts the tab to sleep, nodrift spots the missing time on waking and asks the same question, under the heading System Pause Detected.
  • Midnight rollover. If a shift is still running at midnight, nodrift saves it against the day that just ended and starts a fresh one for the new date. Nothing is lost and nothing lands on the wrong day.

Turning Enable idle lock off stops the first two prompts and lets the timer run without interruption. That is the better setting on a phone, which sits in a pocket generating no typing or scrolling and would otherwise ask you about a gap on nearly every shift. Midnight rollover keeps working either way.

Guards against bad entries

  • One tab at a time. Two copies of nodrift running at once could overwrite each other, so only one is allowed to track. The others show a Multiple Tabs Detected screen with a Take Over Here button.
  • Very short shifts. Ending a shift under 60 seconds asks you to confirm first, in case the button was pressed by accident. You can still choose Log Anyway.

Typing times quickly

Anywhere you type a length of time — the Add Log and Edit forms, the goal, the idle threshold — you can use shorthand and nodrift will tidy it up when you press Enter or click away.

  • 8 becomes 8 hours.
  • 8.5 becomes 8 hours 30 minutes.
  • 45m becomes 45 minutes.
  • 8h 30m becomes 8 hours 30 minutes.

The same applies to start and finish clock times:

  • 0900 or 900 becomes 09:00:00 AM.
  • 900p or 900pm becomes 09:00:00 PM.
  • 9:30 and 9:30p are both understood, and the seconds are filled in.
  • If you leave out AM/PM, anything from 12 upwards is read as PM and anything below 12 as AM.

The "RAM Only" warning

nodrift keeps checking that it can actually save to your browser. If saving fails — private browsing, blocked storage, or a full disk — a red RAM Only badge appears in the top bar. That means your work exists only in memory and will vanish when you close the page. Download a JSON backup straight away.

What Insights shows

Insights is the summary view: how much you have worked over a period, how that compares with your target, and whether you are ahead or behind.

  • Weekly — one bar per weekday, Monday to Friday, measured against the 40-hour week.
  • Monthly — one row per week of the chosen month.
  • Yearly — one row per month of the year.

Switch between the three by clicking Weekly Work at the top of the panel.

Moving between weeks

Use the arrows either side of the date label to step backwards and forwards, and double-click the label itself to jump straight back to today. On a computer, [ and ] do the same thing, and H returns to the current week.

Reading the numbers

  • Weekly Work — hours worked so far against the 40-hour target, with the percentage beside it.
  • Total Break — break time over the same span.
  • Pace Required — the average per day you now need across the working days you have left in order to reach 40 hours. It recalculates as you log time.
  • Status line — a short plain-English verdict, such as how many hours ahead or behind you are.

The day bars

In the weekly view, each bar is one day and fills up as you approach that day's goal. Today's bar keeps moving while a shift is running.

  • A fully green bar means the goal for that day was met.
  • A bar with diagonal stripes is a booked leave day. Leave days are left out of pace and goal maths.
  • Hovering a bar opens a summary of that day: date, work, break, how far over or under goal it was, the goal itself, and any notes you saved.

The letter badges

  • W — work time logged for that shift.
  • B — break time logged for that shift.
  • O — over: the shift met or beat its goal.
  • U — under: the shift fell short of its goal.
  • G — the goal that shift was measured against.

How leave affects the maths

Booking a leave day takes 8 hours off the 40-hour weekly target and marks that date with stripes, so the days around it are not asked to cover for it.

If you end up working on a day you had booked as leave, the hours still count towards your totals and the day is marked Worked Leave — your pace is not penalised either way.

The Consistency Heatmap

The heatmap button in the toolbar opens a calendar of the whole year, one square per day, shaded by how much you worked. It is the quickest way to see streaks and gaps. Use the year label at the top to look at a different year.

  • Hovering a square shows that day's detail. Today's square includes the shift you are running right now.
  • Clicking a square closes the heatmap and takes you to that day in the Logbook, with the filters already set for you.
  • The bottom-left corner shows your year-to-date work hours and how many leave days you have used.

Reading the list

The Logbook holds every shift you have saved, newest first. Each row shows the date, when you started and finished, work and break totals, how you did against that day's goal, and any note you wrote.

Click anywhere on a row to open it for editing. Scroll down a little way and a button appears in the corner to jump back to the top.

Adding a shift by hand

Press Add Log in the Logbook header to enter a day you did not track live.

Fill in any two of Login, Logout and Work and the third is worked out for you. Changing Break updates whichever of the others makes sense. If the break you enter is longer than the shift itself, the field turns red and explains the problem.

Typing dates quickly

Any date field accepts shorthand. Press Enter or click away and it expands to a full date.

  • t, today or 0 — today.
  • y, yesterday or -1 — yesterday.
  • -5 — five days ago, and so on for any number.
  • 15th jan or jan 15 — that date.
  • 12252026 and 122526 both become 25 December 2026; 1225 adds the current year; a bare 15 becomes the 15th of this month.

Editing and deleting

  • The pencil icon opens the entry for editing. Every field can be changed, including the goal that shift was measured against.
  • The bin icon deletes it. You are asked to confirm, and a deleted entry cannot be brought back except from a backup or a snapshot.

Filters and saved views

Filters opens a drawer where you can narrow the list by date, hours or text. Once you have a combination you use often, save it as a named view — it then appears in the dropdown at the top of the drawer and is one click away. Views you have created can be deleted from the same place.

Copying and exporting

  • Copy puts your log history on the clipboard as a tidy plain-text summary, grouped by day, with any shift under 7 hours flagged. Paste it straight into an email.
  • CSV downloads a spreadsheet of the entries you are currently viewing — date, start and finish, work and break hours, goal and notes — ready for Excel or Google Sheets.

Leave and holidays

The Leaves button in the toolbar opens a window with two tabs.

  • Log Leave — pick a date and a type, then press Add Leave Entry. Your booked dates are listed underneath and can be removed from there.
  • Balances — shows each type of leave with its total, how many days you have used and how many are left. Set your own allowances here, and use + Add Leave Type to create a category of your own.

What Tasks is for

Tasks is a small separate stopwatch for timing individual pieces of work inside your day. It runs completely independently of your shift — starting a task does not touch Production Time, and your shift keeps running normally.

Timing a task

  • Type what you are doing in the box at the top, then press Start.
  • Pause stops the clock without ending the task; press it again to carry on.
  • Done saves the task with its start time, finish time, total length and your note.
  • The × in the corner throws the task away without saving it.

Your task history

Finished tasks are listed underneath, grouped by date. The list is built to stay fast no matter how many tasks you have, so it renders only the rows on screen as you scroll.

  • Add Task records a task you did not time, by entering the details yourself.
  • Filters narrows the history by date, length or text, the same way the Logbook filters work.
  • The copy icon on a row copies that one task; the copy button in the header copies them all.
  • CSV downloads the whole task history.

Tasks are included in your JSON backups and come back when you restore one.

Backups

A JSON backup is a single file holding your entire history and settings. It is the only copy that survives clearing your browser data or moving to another device, so keep one somewhere safe and refresh it about once a week.

  • Backup JSON downloads the file. Turn on Auto-save JSON backup in Settings to have one saved automatically each time you end a shift.
  • Restore JSON loads a backup back in. Its entries are merged with what you already have rather than replacing everything.
  • If a restored backup covers days you already have, an Import Conflict window shows both versions side by side and asks whether to keep what is on this device, replace it with the backup, or keep both copies and sort them out yourself.

Settings

The gear button in the toolbar opens the settings panel. Hover over any setting to see a one-line description at the bottom of it.

  • Auto-populate daily goal — lets nodrift set each day's goal to keep you on pace for 40 hours a week. Turn it off to set the goal yourself. It cannot be changed while a shift is running.
  • Enable idle lock — turns the inactivity and system-pause prompts on or off. Off is usually the right choice on a phone.
  • Threshold — how long nodrift waits before deciding you are idle. Type it the same way as any other duration, for example 45m or 1h 30m. It starts at 1 hour, and is only shown while idle lock is on.
  • Auto-save JSON backup — downloads a backup file automatically whenever you end a shift.
  • Auto-email EOD summary — on ending a shift, copies your summary to the clipboard and opens a new email draft ready to paste into.
  • Restore Snapshot — see below.

Snapshots

Before every change to your data, nodrift quietly saves a snapshot of how things looked beforehand. If something goes wrong — a bad edit, a deletion you regret — open Settings, pick a time from the Restore Snapshot list, and everything returns to exactly that moment.

Snapshots live in the same browser as your data, so they cover mistakes, not lost devices. A JSON backup is what covers that.

Theme, time zone and goal presets

  • Theme — the theme button in the top bar offers SF Light, SF Dark, E-Ink and Vercel Dark. Hovering a name previews it; clicking keeps it.
  • Time zone — click the time zone label to switch the main clock between PST, MST, CST and EST. The second clock is always BST, as a fixed reference.
  • Goal presets — click the Daily Goal to open its presets, nudge it with −15m and +15m, or double-click a preset button to save your own amount onto it.

Running two tabs at once

Only one nodrift tab is allowed to track at a time, so two copies can never overwrite each other's work. Any extra tab shows Multiple Tabs Detected. Press Take Over Here in the tab you actually want to use and it takes control, bringing the current state with it.

Starting over

The red Wipe button erases everything — shifts, tasks, leave, saved views, snapshots and settings — and reloads the app, along with any other tabs you have open, so nothing can write the old data back. There is no undo. Download a JSON backup first if there is any chance you will want the data again.

Keyboard shortcuts

These work on a computer with a keyboard. They are ignored while you are typing in a text box, and while the idle prompt is waiting for an answer. There are no shortcuts on a phone.

Tracking

  • Space — start the shift, take a break, or go back to work, depending on what you are doing.
  • S — end the shift and open the save box.
  • Ctrl + S (Cmd + S on a Mac) — download a JSON backup and open an email draft to send it to yourself.
  • Alt + = / Alt + - — raise or lower today's goal by 15 minutes.

Getting around

  • Alt + 1 / 2 / 3 — jump to Insights, Logbook or Tasks.
  • Alt + K — open the Logbook, expand the filters and put the cursor in the search box.
  • Alt + N — add a shift by hand.
  • Alt + T — change theme.
  • ? — open this guide.

Insights

  • [ and ], or Alt + ← / → — step back and forward through the weeks.
  • H — jump back to the current week.

Working through a list

First give the list the keyboard's attention: press Alt + K, or press Tab until a row is highlighted. Then use ↑ and ↓ to move between rows.

With a shift highlighted in the Logbook:

  • E — edit it.
  • C — copy it to the clipboard.
  • N or Enter — read its note.
  • D, Delete or Backspace — delete it, after confirming.

With a task highlighted in Tasks:

  • E or Enter — edit it.
  • C — copy it to the clipboard.
  • D, Delete or Backspace — delete it.

In dialogs

  • Enter — confirms or saves whatever box is open.
  • Escape — leaves a text field, closes the box on top, and clears any highlighted row.
  • Tab — moves between fields, and stays inside the open box rather than wandering off behind it.
